grounded_displacements.note: The machine-derived receiver record (abi.receiver) is bounds_only with offsets [24, 28, 56, 60] = 0x18, 0x1c, 0x38, 0x3c and register ECX. That is a location claim only: it states where the body was seen reaching, not which member sits there. The source therefore writes through the displacement and names no member. The listing's own ECX-operand displacement scan is empty because the body copies ECX to ESI at 0x006a2b22 and addresses the receiver through ESI, so the record is the only witness for these four.
grounded_displacements.register_alias: ESI after MOV ESI,ECX at 0x006a2b22, then ADD ESI,0x18 at 0x006a2b3a, after which [ESI + 0x4] is receiver+0x1c; the source expresses every access as receiver+displacement instead of reproducing the alias

implementation.port_policy: All three direct callees are package-local ports named with their VAs (helper_0092cb00, helper_00612b20, helper_00685a30). No runtime-gated helper or global was promoted to a function record.

No struct with named members is declared for the receiver, because the machine-derived receiver record enumerates displacements and names no member, so any member name would be an ungrounded identity claim.

validation.validation_note: The eight static checks are re-run by the orchestrator; the worker's own run is recorded in the worker result rather than asserted here.

mechanics.behavior: Straight-line, no branch: zero-fill a companion array, run the degenerate range move, run the release pass over the entry range, then rewind the end cursor by a whole number of element strides.
mechanics.fill_call: 0x0092cb00(dest = receiver+0x3c, value = 0, count = receiver+0x38), called first; its return value is discarded
mechanics.move_call: 0x00612b20(first = receiver+0x1c, last = receiver+0x1c, out = receiver+0x18), a degenerate range, so the callee returns its third word, the begin cursor
mechanics.release_call: 0x00685a30(this = receiver+0x18, first = the move call's return, last = receiver+0x1c re-read after the move)
mechanics.receiver_self_comparison: none - the body never compares against its own receiver and has no early exit
mechanics.span_subtraction: byte subtraction of the two cursors taken from registers loaded before either call, not from the re-read memory word
mechanics.stack_cleanup: one ADD ESP,0x18 at 0x006a2b48 removes six words, the three argument words of each of the two cdecl calls; the release port removes its own two words with RET 0x8
state_reads: receiver+0x38 (fill word, pushed as the count)
receiver+0x3c (fill word, pushed as the destination)
receiver+0x1c (end cursor), read twice: once at 0x006a2b37 into EDI and once at 0x006a2b45 into EDX
state_writes: the companion array at receiver+0x38 / receiver+0x3c, through the 0x0092cb00 fill (indirect: the words themselves are not written by this body)
receiver+0x1c (end cursor) via ADD dword ptr [ESI + 0x4],EAX
flow: Load the two words at receiver+0x38 and receiver+0x3c and call 0x0092cb00 with them and a zero, discarding the result.
Load the begin cursor from receiver+0x18 and the end cursor from receiver+0x1c.
Call 0x00612b20 with the degenerate range (end, end, begin); it returns the begin cursor.
Re-read the end cursor from receiver+0x1c and call 0x00685a30 with receiver+0x18 as receiver, the returned cursor as first word and the re-read end cursor as second word.
Compute trunc((end - begin) / 0x18) with the 0xd5555555 multiply-shift sequence and add the quotient times 0x18 to the end cursor at receiver+0x1c.

observed_mechanics: 0x006a2b20..0x006a2b22: PUSH EBX; PUSH ESI; MOV ESI,ECX - the receiver arrives in ECX and is kept in ESI; no argument word is ever read from the stack.
0x006a2b24: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x38] - a word of the receiver is loaded into EAX and immediately pushed, so it is an argument rather than a value this body keeps.
0x006a2b27: MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x3c] - a second word of the receiver is loaded into ECX and pushed as the first argument.

0x006a2b2a..0x006a2b2f: PUSH EDI; PUSH EAX; PUSH 0x0; PUSH ECX; CALL 0x0092cb00 - three cdecl words (word+0x3c, the immediate 0x0, word+0x38). The callee body computes dest + count*4 and, while that end is above dest, stores the value word repeatedly from dest, then returns dest in EAX; the result is discarded, EAX being reloaded at 0x006a2b34.
0x006a2b34: MOV EBX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x18] - the begin cursor of the entry range.
0x006a2b37: MOV EDI,dword ptr [ESI + 0x1c] - the end cursor of the entry range.

0x006a2b3a: ADD ESI,0x18 - ESI stops being the receiver base; it is reused as the second call's thiscall receiver and as the base of the [ESI + 0x4] load at 0x006a2b45 and the [ESI + 0x4] store at 0x006a2b70, both of which are therefore receiver+0x1c.

0x006a2b3d..0x006a2b40: PUSH EBX; PUSH EDI; PUSH EDI; CALL 0x00612b20 - the pushed range is degenerate because the first two words are the same register, so the callee's compare-and-loop is never entered and its third word, the begin cursor, is returned in EAX.
0x006a2b45: MOV EDX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x4] - the end cursor is re-read from memory after the move rather than reused from EDI.
0x006a2b48: ADD ESP,0x18 - one cleanup removes six words: the three argument words of 0x0092cb00 and the three of 0x00612b20. Both callees are therefore cdecl and the caller owns their stack.

0x006a2b4b..0x006a2b4f: PUSH EDX; PUSH EAX; MOV ECX,ESI; CALL 0x00685a30 - the release helper receives receiver+0x18 as its thiscall receiver, the move call's return as its first word and the re-read end cursor as its second word; its own RET 0x8 removes those two words.
0x006a2b54: SUB EDI,EBX - a byte subtraction of the two cursors captured before either call, not an element count.
0x006a2b56..0x006a2b5b: MOV EAX,0xd5555555; IMUL EDI - a signed 32x32 multiply whose high half lands in EDX.
0x006a2b5d..0x006a2b65: SAR EDX,0x2; MOV EAX,EDX; SHR EAX,0x1f; ADD EAX,EDX - an arithmetic shift by two plus a sign-bit correction, i.e. a truncating division of the byte span by the element stride.
0x006a2b67..0x006a2b6e: LEA EAX,[EAX + EAX*0x2] then ADD EAX,EAX three times - the corrected quotient scaled by three and then by eight, giving the quotient times the 0x18 element stride.

0x006a2b70: ADD dword ptr [ESI + 0x4],EAX - the product is added to the end cursor, so for a span that is a whole number of strides the end cursor is rewound onto the begin cursor and the range is emptied.
0x006a2b73..0x006a2b76: POP EDI; POP ESI; POP EBX; RET - a bare RET with no immediate, and a frame balanced by the single ADD ESP,0x18, confirming a thiscall with no explicit stack arguments.
The complete 39-instruction body contains no conditional branch, no indirect transfer and no data-segment address: the three CALL immediates are the only control transfers out.

observed_original_abi.reason: The machine body copies ECX to ESI at 0x006a2b22 before any write to it, never reads an argument word from the stack, and ends in a bare RET with no immediate. The persisted Ghidra signature for the target is void App::DirectPropertyList::Clear(DirectPropertyList * this) with the receiver in ECX. The machine-derived envelope agrees (__thiscall, receiver ECX, ret_form RET, stack_cleanup_bytes 0, owner caller).
observed_original_abi.return_semantics_disagreement: The machine-derived envelope classifies the last EAX write as pointer_like_in_EAX and its return.type is null with void_possible false. That classification is a register-shape inference over the rewind byte count, which the body stores through receiver+0x1c at 0x006a2b70 before the epilogue; no value is transferred to the caller. void is the claim this record makes, on the strength of the bare RET, the resolved Ghidra prototype and the SDK label. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved.

ownership_reconfirmation.result: No metadata record for 0x006a2b20 existed under reconstruction/metadata before this write, and no staging file named it. The sibling body 0x006a2a80 (App::PropertyList::Clear) is held by other packages and was read only; nothing of theirs was modified.

unresolved_questions: The identity of the receiver words at 0x18, 0x1c, 0x38 and 0x3c. The machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only and enumerates displacements, not members, so the candidate deliberately names none. A layout naming these words needs a source outside this body (the SDK header, or a writer elsewhere in the binary).

The meaning of the pair at receiver+0x38 and receiver+0x3c. The 0x0092cb00 body fills count consecutive dwords at dest with a value word and returns dest, so the shape is a (count, destination) pair for a companion array, but whether that array is parallel to the 0x18-stride entry range, indexed by the same stride, or unrelated is not observable from this body.
Whether the immediate 0x0 pushed as the fill value is a null pointer or a zero fill word. The callee stores it as a dword with a repeated store, so only its 32-bit value is claimed.

Whether the byte span at receiver+0x18..0x1c is always an exact multiple of the 0x18 stride. The rewind only lands on the begin cursor when it is; for a ragged span the end cursor is rewound to the nearest lower stride boundary.
The real body and general contract of 0x0092cb00 beyond the dword fill, and of 0x00612b20 beyond the 0x18-stride move and its degenerate-range return.
The release call 0x00685a30 makes per qualifying entry (0x0093db80 on the sub-object at entry+4, gated on byte entry+0x14 bit 0x4), and what that sub-object owns.

The return-type disagreement recorded in observed_original_abi: the machine-derived envelope calls the last EAX write pointer_like while this record claims void. Resolving it needs either a caller-side use of EAX or a source outside this binary.
Whether the shared vtable 0x01408870 dispatches this body at a fixed slot, and which callers reach it. The record carries one vtable xref and no direct caller xref.
The concrete layout of the receiver between offsets 0x00 and 0x17, and between 0x20 and 0x37, which this body never touches.
